results.fact: Ghana's 2024 anti-LGBTQ 'Human Sexuality' bill lapsed unsigned when Parliament dissolved pre-2024 election; colonial 'unnatural carnal knowledge' criminalisation persists; Pres. Mahama signalled willingness to sign a reintroduced bill
Legal since 1993, equal age of consent 2012, civil pacts 2014, same-sex marriage since 2016, SO+gender-reassignment protections since 2007; no legal gender recognition
Criminalised: art. 274 of the 2016 Penal Code, 6 months–3 years or fine; no legal gender recognition; limited protections
2022 Penal Code made same-sex sexual activity LEGAL and added Equatorial Guinea's first explicit sexual-orientation employment protections; legal gender change still not recognised
Still criminalised (S.158, up to 14 years; women added 2005; 2014 'aggravated homosexuality' carries life; no legal gender change)
Marriage equality upheld by Supreme Court May 2025 (ruling published March 2026); self-ID gender recognition since 2010, depathologised 2017; NEW Apr 2025 surrogacy ban for gay/single men
Full French framework applies: decriminalised 1791, marriage 2013, no-surgery self-declaration gender recognition (2017); locally higher violent crime, visible tourism economy
LegCo VETOED the government's registered-partnerships bill 71–14 (Sept 2025) after the Sep-2025 court deadline; legal gender recognition still requires full sex reassignment surgery
2020 legal-gender-change ban stands (explicitly illegal); 2021 'child protection' law in force; NEW: March 2025 law bans organising/participating in Pride — Budapest Pride permit denied 3 June 2025
New national penal code EFFECTIVE 2 January 2026: criminalises sex outside marriage (≤1 yr) and obscenity articles explicitly cover same-sex acts; first enforcement — 25 sentenced May 2026
Stable: civil partnerships 2011, same-sex marriage since 2016 (the 2015-16 legalisation completed), gender-recognition right since 2009, 'gender reassignment' protections
